text:
sara: deploy-bot just auto-rolled back the embeddings route in canary (12:04 UTC) citing error_rate_threshold. I see an uptick in 5xxs for /v1/embeddings only, not generation.
deploy-bot: autopilot: detected error_rate > 2% on route /v1/embeddings for 4 minutes; initiated safe rollback to v4.1.3 for that route. Rollout id: 0xabc7.
tom: grafana snapshot: https://grafana.internal/snap/xyz 914 seems isolated to host shard B and a single kernel upgrade batch.
liam: Sentry shows timeouts from the internal kv store during embedding batching. Could be a gradual mempressure event on shared pools.
anna: note: reserved/dedicated pools unaffected per our checks. Only shared canary traffic slice hit.
sara: proposal: instead of full-service rollback, do a targeted route-level rollback for /v1/embeddings and pin service-level rollout so we don't ramp. Also notify customers in release-notes and support. Thoughts?
tom: +1 for targeted rollback. We should also flip the feature-flag `embeddings_v2` to off for ephemeral slices while infra looks. That avoids touching customers pinned to older versions.
liam: ops command ready: `deploy-bot rollback --service api-service --version v4.1.3 --route '/v1/embeddings' --rollout 0xabc7 --reason "kv-timeouts"`
sara: anna, can you confirm traffic split config for the canary? I want to ensure we only roll back the 5% embeddings slice.
anna: confirmed: canary embeddings slice = 5% traffic, host shard B. Setting feature-flag and performing targeted rollback now.
deploy-bot: executing targeted rollback... done. Route /v1/embeddings reverted to v4.1.3 for rollout 0xabc7. Note: service remains at v4.2.0 for other routes.
liam: running `rb set-flag embeddings_v2 off --scope canary --duration 20m` and `rb monitor --rollout 0xabc7 --routes /v1/embeddings --metric error_rate --window 5m`
tom: I'm handing this: will watch error_rate and p95 for the route. If error_rate > 1% for 10m we do a service-level manual rollback.
sara: comms: Paul in support wants a short note for customers and a separate internal blurb for enterprise accounts. I'll draft. Can someone trigger release-notes-bot to post a customer-safe line?
release-notes-bot: draft ready: "We observed elevated errors affecting embeddings during a phased rollout; we've rolled back the embeddings route while we investigate. No dedicated customer pools impacted. If you rely on embeddings, expect brief retries; contact support with case RL-1302."
anna: posting to #release-notes now. Link: https://slack.internal/release-notes/MSG1234
liam: ops: check reserved pools again? I want to be extra sure no auto-traffic leak happened.
anna: verified reserved pools: none received canary traffic. We also set a hard pin: `rb pin-rollout 0xabc7 --hold` so autopilot won't resume.
sara: timeline: pause autopilot + route rollback (done), feature-flag off, monitor 15m, if stable -> unpin and resume rollout for embeddings; if not -> escalate to manual service rollback and schedule a customer update. Owners: liam (metrics+kv traces), tom (engineering rollback verification), anna (comms posting + pin).
tom: I'll gather kernel upgrade batch logs and check the host group's recent packages: `ansible -i hosts_b kernel:status` then paste findings.
liam: collecting kv traces: `curl $TRACE_API/rollouts/0xabc7?route=%2Fv1%2Fembeddings | jq .spans` and forwarding to infra.
anna: pinned rollout 0xabc7 (pin-id: pin-991). Autopilot paused for 30m.
sara: reminder for comms: update enterprise customers if we don't resolve in 30m. Paul (support) has template, will send if we hit the window.
tom: note on rollback strategy: targeted route rollbacks are preferred when a single route regresses. Avoids broad service blips. Documenting this in the runbook after postmortem.
liam: monitoring shows error_rate back to baseline at t+8m for the route. Will keep watching for full 15m period.
anna: release-notes-bot posted customer blurb; support ticket RL-1302 created and linked.
sara: flagging this as resolved-for-now. We'll reopen if errors reappear or if infra finds a host regression. Good job everyone. :tada:
